question: What defines a community health problem compared to an individual illness?

options.A: It can only be diagnosed using laboratory blood tests
options.B: It only occurs inside rural village settlements
options.C: It strictly affects people over the age of sixty years
options.D: It affects groups of people and often shares environmental or social roots

explanation: Community health problems involve populations rather than single patients, often tied to shared living conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h1)

question: Why must a public health nurse look beyond single patients when studying a community?

options.A: To ensure that doctors do not interfere with community nursing duties
options.B: So that the nurse can prescribe drugs without a medical doctor present
options.C: To spot wider patterns of disease linked to shared environmental or economic factors
options.D: Because individual hospital records are completely useless for public health

explanation: Looking at the bigger picture reveals systemic issues affecting the whole population, not just isolated cases. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of problem identification in community health?

options.A: To close down traditional healing centers in the community
options.B: To punish local leaders who fail to clean their environment
options.C: To write medical prescriptions for every household in the ward
options.D: To discover and define health gaps within a target population

explanation: Problem identification focuses on finding and describing unmet health needs so they can be addressed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h2)

question: Why is assuming a community's health needs based only on past experience a major mistake?

options.A: Every community has unique conditions, and unverified assumptions lead to wasted resources
options.B: Illnesses never repeat themselves in the same geographic location twice
options.C: Community members prefer foreign nurses to local healthcare workers
options.D: Past experience is legally forbidden in public health practice

explanation: Relying on assumptions instead of current local data often results in interventions that do not match real community needs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of primary data collection?

options.A: Reviewing old hospital admission registers in the record room
options.B: Conducting house-to-house surveys and interviews with residents
options.C: Reading national census reports published ten years ago
options.D: Downloading international World Health Organization PDF reports

explanation: Primary data is gathered directly from the source by the healthcare worker conducting the investigation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of combining both primary and secondary data sources?

options.A: It allows the nurse to finish community work without visiting the field
options.B: It prevents community members from asking questions about healthcare
options.C: It gives a balanced and realistic view of local health realities by cross-checking facts
options.D: It guarantees that government funding will double immediately

explanation: Using multiple sources helps verify findings and provides a thorough picture of community health status. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h3)

question: What three core elements are typically included in a community diagnosis statement?

options.A: The political party in power, the village chief, and tax rates
options.B: The weather forecast, the road network, and transport costs
options.C: The health problem, the affected population, and the contributing factors
options.D: The name of the nurse, the hospital budget, and drug expiration dates

explanation: A complete community diagnosis clearly names the issue, who is suffering from it, and why it is happening. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h4)

question: A public health nurse writes a summary stating that teenage mothers in a rural ward have high rates of anemia due to poor nutrition and lack of antenatal care. What is this process called?
explanation: Synthesizing data to identify health deficits, vulnerable groups, and causes in a population is known as a community diagnosis. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h4)

question: Why is community participation essential during problem identification?

options.A: It ensures that traditional rulers make all medical diagnoses
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to visit households in person
options.C: It allows community members to pay the salaries of health workers
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures real priorities are addressed

explanation: Involving locals guarantees that the actual needs of the people are uncovered and that they will support the intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h5)

question: What usually happens when health professionals bypass community input and decide problems alone?

options.A: Government funding increases because the staff showed independence
options.B: The community completes all health projects much faster
options.C: They often target issues that do not match the real priorities of the residents
options.D: Local disease rates drop instantly due to professional expertise

explanation: Without local consultation, healthcare workers may focus on problems that matter to textbooks rather than the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h5)

question: Which criterion measures how many people in a population are affected by a health issue?
explanation: Magnitude refers to the sheer size or frequency of the health problem within the population. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h6)

question: Why is prioritization necessary after collecting community health data?

options.A: Government regulations forbid treating more than one disease at a time
options.B: Minor health issues are completely unimportant and should be ignored forever
options.C: It helps nurses avoid doing any field work for the rest of the year
options.D: Resources like time and money are limited, so the most urgent issues must be tackled first

explanation: Because resources are finite, prioritization ensures the most pressing and impactful health problems receive attention first. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of translating a community problem into a formal nursing diagnosis?

options.A: To replace all medical doctors in the primary healthcare center
options.B: To hide community health failures from government inspectors
options.C: To increase the cost of health services for local residents
options.D: To bridge data collection and structure a focused, goal-oriented care plan

explanation: A formal nursing diagnosis turns raw findings into a clear statement that guides planning and intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h7)

question: How does a community-level nursing diagnosis differ from an individual patient diagnosis?

options.A: It is written by traditional rulers instead of trained nursing personnel
options.B: It ignores environmental factors and concentrates purely on gene mutations
options.C: It describes health patterns and risks affecting an entire group or population
options.D: It focuses only on surgical complications inside a hospital operating theater

explanation: Community nursing diagnoses address population-wide health issues and collective responses rather than single patients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective community health data collection in Nigeria?

options.A: An excess of modern computers in every rural primary health clinic
options.B: Too many trained nurses working in remote village settlements
options.C: Inadequate funding, difficult terrain, and security challenges
options.D: Strict laws that ban community surveys across all local governments

explanation: Logistical hurdles, funding shortages, and security risks often complicate health assessments in the field. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h8)

question: Why can cultural beliefs and stigma create obstacles during problem identification?

options.A: Stigma forces communities to build private hospitals for themselves
options.B: Local customs automatically cure all infectious diseases without treatment
options.C: Residents may hide health issues or distrust outside health workers
options.D: Traditional rulers refuse to let nurses keep written records

explanation: Fear of stigma and lack of trust in outsiders can prevent community members from sharing true health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h8)
